key_provisions_or_claims: Intelligent robots could theoretically acquire moral and human rights under plausible assumptions.
Dissimilarities between humans and robots create epistemic challenges for attributing rights.
Hard to distinguish genuine artificial rights-holders from robotic moral zombies.
Critically examines assumptions of both robot-rights skeptics and proponents.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper from Robophilosophy 2024 examining whether robots could bear human rights under the human rights approach. It analyses foundational assumptions, implications for future robots and practical challenges, concluding that rights are theoretically possible but epistemic problems make identifying genuine artificial rights-holders from 'moral zombies' difficult.
annotation.title_clean: Applying the Human Rights Approach to Robots: Possibilities and Challenges
annotation.title_en: Applying the Human Rights Approach to Robots: Possibilities and Challenges
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 397 (Robophilosophy 2024), IOS Press
